title: 'The Fall of the House of Usher,' by Edgar Allan Poe, Part One
titleZh: 爱伦·坡的《厄舍屋的倒塌》第一部分

sentences.en: It was a dark and soundless day near the end of the year, and clouds were hanging low in the heavens.
sentences.zh: 那是年底时分一个阴暗而寂静的日子，乌云低低地压在天空。

sentences.en: All day I had been riding on horseback through country with little life or beauty; and in the early evening, I came within view of the House of Usher.
sentences.zh: 我一整天都骑马穿行在几乎毫无生气、也毫无美景的乡间；到了傍晚时分，我望见了罗宅的轮廓。

sentences.en: I do not know how it was — but, with my first sight of the building, a sense of heavy sadness filled my spirit.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是怎么回事——可是，当我第一眼看到那座房子时，一种沉重的悲伤便涌上了我的心头。

sentences.en: I looked at the scene before me — at the house itself — at the ground around it — at the cold stone walls of the building — at its empty eye-like windows — and at a few dead trees — I looked at this scene, I say, with a complete sadness of soul, which was no healthy, earthly feeling.
sentences.zh: 我望着眼前的景象——望着那座房子本身——望着它四周的场地——望着它冰冷的石墙——望着它那双空洞的、宛如眼睛般的窗户——望着几棵枯死的树木——我这样说吧，我带着一种彻骨的悲伤凝望着这景象，那是一种不健康、不属于尘世的感受。

sentences.en: There was a coldness, a sickening of the heart, in which I could discover nothing to lighten the weight I felt.
sentences.zh: 那是一种寒意，一种令人心悸的沉郁，在其中我找不到任何能减轻我心头重量的东西。

sentences.en: What was it, I asked myself, what was it that was so fearful, so frightening in my view of the House of Usher?
sentences.zh: 我暗自问自己：在我眼中，罗宅究竟有什么东西如此可怕、如此令人恐惧？

sentences.en: This was a question to which I could find no answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我找不到答案的问题。

sentences.en: I stopped my horse beside the building, on the edge of a dark and quiet lake.
sentences.zh: 我把马停在房子旁边，就停在那片幽暗而平静的湖水边缘。

sentences.en: There, I could see reflected in the water a clear picture of the dead trees, and of the house and its empty, eye-like windows.
sentences.zh: 在那里，我能看到水中倒映着枯树、房子以及它那双空洞的、宛如眼睛般的窗户的清晰画面。

sentences.en: I was now going to spend several weeks in this house of sadness — this house of gloom.
sentences.zh: 我即将在这座悲伤之屋——这座阴郁之屋——里度过好几个星期。

sentences.en: Its owner was named Roderick Usher.
sentences.zh: 它的主人名叫罗德里克·罗。

sentences.en: We had been friends when we were boys; but many years had passed since our last meeting.
sentences.zh: 我们少年时曾是朋友；可自上次相聚以来，已经过去了许多年。

sentences.en: A letter from him had reached me; a wild letter, which demanded that I reply by coming to see him.
sentences.zh: 他寄来了一封信，一封狂野的信，信中要求我亲自来探望他作为回应。

sentences.en: He wrote of an illness of the body — of a sickness of the mind — and of a desire to see me — his best and, indeed, his only friend.
sentences.zh: 他写道自己身患疾病——心智也生了病——并渴望见到我——他最好的、 indeed 唯一的朋友。

sentences.en: It was the manner in which all this was said — it was the heart in it — which did not allow me to say no.
sentences.zh: 正是这一切被说出的方式——正是其中蕴含的真情——让我无法说“不”。

sentences.en: Although as boys we had been together, I really knew little about my friend.
sentences.zh: 尽管少年时我们曾在一起，可我对这位朋友其实知之甚少。

sentences.en: I knew, however, that his family, a very old one, had long been famous for its understanding of all the arts, and for many quiet acts of kindness to the poor.
sentences.zh: 不过我知道，他的家族是一个极其古老的家族，长久以来以精通各种艺术而闻名，并因许多默默的善举而深受穷人的敬重。

sentences.en: I had learned, too, that the family had never been a large one, with many branches.
sentences.zh: 我也了解到，这个家族从来都不庞大，没有众多的分支。

sentences.en: The name had passed always from father to son, and when people spoke of the “House of Usher,” they included both the family and the family home.
sentences.zh: 这个姓氏一直由父亲传给儿子，当人们谈起“罗宅”时，他们既指这个家族，也指这处家族宅邸。

sentences.en: I again looked up from the picture of the house reflected in the lake to the house itself.
sentences.zh: 我又一次从湖中房子的倒影抬起头，望向房子本身。

sentences.en: A strange idea grew in my mind — an idea so strange that I tell it only to show the force of the feelings which laid their weight on me.
sentences.zh: 一个奇怪的想法在我心中萌生——这个想法如此奇怪，我讲出来只是为了表明那种压在我心头的力量的强度。

sentences.en: I really believed that around the whole house, and the ground around it, the air itself was different.
sentences.zh: 我真的相信，在整座房子周围，以及房子周围的地面，连空气本身都变得不同。

sentences.en: It was not the air of heaven.
sentences.zh: 那不是天堂的空气。

sentences.en: It rose from the dead, decaying trees, from the gray walls, and the quiet lake.
sentences.zh: 它从那些死去的、腐烂的树木中升起，从灰色的墙壁中升起，从宁静的湖水中升起。

sentences.en: It was a sickly, unhealthy air that I could see, slow-moving, heavy, and gray.
sentences.zh: 那是一种病态的、不健康的空气，我能看得见，移动缓慢，沉重而灰暗。

sentences.en: Shaking off from my spirit what must have been a dream, I looked more carefully at the building itself.
sentences.zh: 我甩掉精神上那想必是一场梦境的东西，更仔细地打量起这座建筑本身。

sentences.en: The most noticeable thing about it seemed to be its great age.
sentences.zh: 它最引人注目的地方似乎是它悠久的年代。

sentences.en: None of the walls had fallen, yet the stones appeared to be in a condition of advanced decay.
sentences.zh: 没有一面墙壁倒塌，然而那些石头看起来已处于严重腐朽的状态。

sentences.en: Perhaps the careful eye would have discovered the beginning of a break in the front of the building, a crack making its way from the top down the wall until it became lost in the dark waters of the lake.
sentences.zh: 或许细心的眼睛会发现建筑正面开始的一处断裂，一道裂缝从顶部沿着墙壁向下延伸，直到消失在湖水的黑暗深处。

sentences.en: I rode over a short bridge to the house.
sentences.zh: 我骑过一座短桥，来到房子前。

sentences.en: A man who worked in the house — a servant — took my horse, and I entered.
sentences.zh: 一个在屋里做工的人——一个仆人——接过了我的马，我便走了进去。

sentences.en: Another servant, of quiet step, led me without a word through many dark turnings to the room of his master.
sentences.zh: 另一个脚步轻悄的仆人，一言不发地领着我，穿过许多幽暗的转弯，来到他主人的房间。

sentences.en: Much that I met on the way added, I do not know how, to the strangeness of which I have already spoken.
sentences.zh: 一路上我所遇到的一切，不知怎地，都为我前面已经说过的种种怪诞增添了色彩。

sentences.en: While the objects around me — the dark wall coverings, the blackness of the floors, and the things brought home from long forgotten wars — while these things were like the things I had known since I was a baby — while I admitted that all this was only what I had expected — I was still surprised at the strange ideas which grew in my mind from these simple things.
sentences.zh: 当我周围的事物——深色的墙饰、漆黑的地板，以及那些从早已被遗忘的战争中带回的物品——当我发现这些事物与我自婴儿时代起所熟悉的事物一模一样时——当我承认这一切都只是我所预料到的时候——我仍然为这些寻常事物在我心中引发的种种怪诞想法而感到惊讶。

sentences.en: The room I came into was very large and high.
sentences.zh: 我走进的房间非常大，也非常高。

sentences.en: The windows were high, and pointed at the top, and so far above the black floor that they were quite out of reach.
sentences.zh: 窗户开得很高，顶部呈尖形，离漆黑的地板如此遥远，以致完全够不着。

sentences.en: Only a little light, red in color, made its way through the glass, and served to lighten the nearer and larger objects.
sentences.zh: 只有一缕微弱的、泛着红光的灯光，透过玻璃照进来，姑且照亮了近处较大的物体。

sentences.en: My eyes, however, tried and failed to see into the far, high corners of the room.
sentences.zh: 然而，我的眼睛却竭力想看清房间远处高处的角落，却失败了。

sentences.en: Dark coverings hung upon the walls.
sentences.zh: 深色的墙饰悬挂在墙壁上。

sentences.en: The many chairs and tables had been used for a long, long time.
sentences.zh: 那些众多的椅子和桌子，已经被使用了很久很久。

sentences.en: Books lay around the room, but could give it no sense of life.
sentences.zh: 书籍散落在房间各处，却无法为这里增添一丝生气。

sentences.en: I felt sadness hanging over everything.
sentences.zh: 我感到一种悲伤笼罩着一切。

sentences.en: No escape from this deep, cold gloom seemed possible.
sentences.zh: 似乎不可能从这深沉、阴冷的忧郁中逃脱。

sentences.en: As I entered the room, Usher stood up from where he had been lying and met me with a warmth, which at first I could not believe was real.
sentences.zh: 当我进入房间时，夏特从他躺卧的地方起身，以一种起初我几乎不敢相信为真的热情迎接我。

sentences.en: A look, however, at his face told me that every word he spoke was true.
sentences.zh: 然而，只需看看他的面容，我就知道他说的每一句话都是真的。

sentences.en: We sat down; and for some moments, while he said nothing, I looked at him with a feeling of sad surprise.
sentences.zh: 我们坐了下来；有几秒钟，他一言不发，我带着一种悲伤的惊讶注视着他。

sentences.en: Surely, no man had ever before changed as Roderick Usher had!
sentences.zh: certainly，从来没有人像罗德里克·夏特那样改变过！

sentences.en: Could this be the friend of my early years?
sentences.zh: 这难道是我早年的朋友吗？

sentences.en: It is true that his face had always been unusual.
sentences.zh: 确实，他的面容一向很不寻常。

sentences.en: He had gray-white skin; eyes large and full of light; lips not bright in color, but of a beautiful shape; a well-shaped nose; hair of great softness — a face that was not easy to forget.
sentences.zh: 他有着灰白的皮肤；大而明亮的眼睛；颜色不鲜艳却形状优美的嘴唇；轮廓分明的鼻子；极其柔软的头发——一张令人难以忘却的脸。

sentences.en: And now the increase in this strangeness of his face had caused so great a change that I almost did not know him.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这种面容的怪异程度加剧，造成了如此巨大的变化，我几乎认不出他了。

sentences.en: The horrible white of his skin, and the strange light in his eyes, surprised me and even made me afraid.
sentences.zh: 他皮肤那可怕的苍白，以及眼中奇异的光彩，让我感到惊讶，甚至让我有些害怕。

sentences.en: His hair had been allowed to grow, and in its softness it did not fall around his face, but seemed to lie upon the air.
sentences.zh: 他的头发任其生长，那柔软的发丝并不垂落在脸庞四周，而似乎悬浮于空中。

sentences.en: I could not, even with an effort, see in my friend the appearance of a simple human being.
sentences.zh: 我即使竭力，也无法在朋友身上看出一个普通人的模样。

sentences.en: In his manner, I saw at once, changes came and went; and I soon found that this resulted from his attempt to quiet a very great nervousness.
sentences.zh: 从他的举止中，我立刻看到变化忽来忽去；很快我发现，这是由于他试图平息一种极大的神经质。

sentences.en: I had indeed been prepared for something like this, partly by his letter and partly by remembering him as a boy.
sentences.zh: 我确实已为类似这样的情况做好了准备，一部分源于他的来信，一部分源于我记忆中那个男孩的模样。

sentences.en: His actions were first too quick and then too quiet.
sentences.zh: 他的动作先是过于急促，然后又过于安静。

sentences.en: Sometimes his voice, slow and trembling with fear, quickly changed to a strong, heavy, carefully spaced, too perfectly controlled manner.
sentences.zh: 有时，他那缓慢而因恐惧而颤抖的声音，会迅速转变为一种雄壮、沉重、刻意停顿、控制得过于完美的方式。

sentences.en: It was in this manner that he spoke of the purpose of my visit, of his desire to see me, and of the deep delight and strength he expected me to give him.
sentences.zh: 他正是以这种方式谈到了我来访的目的、他渴望见到我，以及他期望我给予他的深切愉悦与力量。

sentences.en: He told me what he believed to be the nature of his illness.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我他所认为的自身疾病的本质。

sentences.en: It was, he said, a family sickness, and one from which he could not hope to grow better — but it was, he added at once, only a nervous illness, which would without doubt soon pass away.
sentences.zh: 他说，这是一种家族病，一种他无法指望好转的病——但他立刻补充道，这不过是一种神经方面的疾病，毫无疑问很快就会过去。

sentences.en: It showed itself in a number of strange feelings.
sentences.zh: 它以种种奇怪的感觉表现出来。

sentences.en: Some of these, as he told me of them, interested me but were beyond my understanding; perhaps the way in which he told me of them added to their strangeness.
sentences.zh: 其中一些，当他向我讲述时，引起了我的兴趣，却超出了我的理解范围；也许他讲述的方式反而增加了这些感觉的奇怪之处。

sentences.en: He suffered much from a sickly increase in the feeling of all his senses; he could eat only the most tasteless food; all flowers smelled too strongly for his nose; his eyes were hurt by even a little light; and there were few sounds which did not fill him with horror.
sentences.zh: 他的所有感官都因一种病态的亢进而饱受折磨：他只能吃最寡淡的食物；所有花香对他来说都太浓烈；哪怕一点点光也会刺痛他的眼睛；几乎没有哪种声音不会让他感到恐惧。

sentences.en: A certain kind of sick fear was completely his master.
sentences.zh: 某种特定类型的病态恐惧完全支配着他。

sentences.en: “I shall die,” he said.
sentences.zh: “我会死的，”他说。

sentences.en: “I shall die!
sentences.zh: “我会死的！

sentences.en: I must die of this fool’s sickness.
sentences.zh: 我必会因这愚蠢的病而死。

sentences.en: In this way, this way and no other way, I shall be lost.
sentences.zh: 就这样，就这样，别无他法，我终将毁灭。

sentences.en: I fear what will happen in the future, not for what happens, but for the result of what happens.
sentences.zh: 我畏惧未来，不是因为将要发生的事，而是因为事情发生后的结果。

sentences.en: I have, indeed, no fear of pain, but only fear of its result — of terror!
sentences.zh: 我确实并不畏惧痛苦，只畏惧它的结果——那恐怖！

sentences.en: I feel that my time will soon arrive when I must lose my life, and my mind, and my soul, together, in some last battle with that horrible enemy: fear!”
sentences.zh: 我感到，我失去生命的时刻即将到来，届时我将连同我的心智与灵魂，在那场与那可怕敌人的最后决战中一同丧失：那就是恐惧！”

glossary.def: to show the image of something on a surface
a condition of being unhealthy in your body or mind
a part of a tree that grows out from the trunk
to be slowly destroyed by natural processes
either one of the two soft parts that surround the mouth
